questions.question: In the Brønsted–Lowry model, what does an acid do?
choices: Accepts a proton
Donates a proton
Donates an electron pair without transferring H+
Releases hydroxide as its defining role

questions.question: In the Brønsted–Lowry model, what does a base do?
choices: Donates a proton
Accepts a proton
Must contain hydrogen but cannot accept H+
Increases hydronium concentration by proton donation

Which ion is used to describe acidity in aqueous solutions?
choices: Hydronium, H3O+
Sodium, Na+
Chloride, Cl−
Calcium, Ca2+

questions.question: What does an acid–base indicator do?
choices: Directly identifies every dissolved chemical
Makes every solution reach pH 7
Changes color over a particular pH range
Measures only the solution's total volume

questions.question: Which term describes an acid that ionizes almost completely in dilute water solution?
choices: Concentrated acid
Weak base
Neutral salt
Strong acid

questions.question: What is a buffer designed to do?

Resist changes in pH after small acid or base additions
Remove all dissolved ions from aqueous solutions
Maintain a fixed temperature during every reaction

questions.question: What does a lower pH indicate when comparing aqueous solutions?

Greater total solution volume
Greater hydronium concentration
Smaller solvent mass

questions.question: Why are strong and concentrated different descriptions of an acid?

Strength concerns color; concentration concerns ionization
Every strong acid must be concentrated

Only oxygen gas forms
The atoms disappear
A new element forms

questions.question: Why is tasting an unknown laboratory solution an unsuitable way to identify an acid?
choices: Taste provides a precise numerical pH
Every dilute acid is safe to taste
It creates an unnecessary exposure risk
Only bases can be hazardous to taste

questions.question: How does diluting an unbuffered acidic solution with water generally change its pH?

It moves toward neutral pH
It must become strongly basic
It becomes independent of hydronium concentration

questions.question: Why can a weak acid solution still have a low pH?

Low pH is determined only by solution volume
Weak acid means low concentration by definition

It must become a neutral solvent molecule
It becomes its conjugate base

Neutrality requires no hydronium or hydroxide ions

100 times
5 times
10 times

pH 3 and pH 5

The solutions must both be neutral

choices: Base
Acid
Conjugate acid of X before transfer
